newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: China finances Sao Tome projects, debt relief.
newsitem.headline: China finances Sao Tome projects, debt relief.

text.p: China agreed on Wednesday to finance imports and construction projects worth $2 million in Sao Tome and Principe and give the empoverished twin island state more time to pay its debts.
The agreements were signed by Foreign Minister Qian Qichen at the start of a two-day visit to the archipelago, 200 km (125 miles) off the coast of Gabon.
Qichen told journalists that China also planned to build a hydroelectric dam on Sao Tome to overcome an energy shortage that was severely limiting development.
China agreed to extend the grace period for a further two years on some $11 million, repayment of which should have begun two years ago.
Sao Tome and Principe owes a total $20 million to China, which is the country's third largest trading partner after Portugal, the former colonial power, and France.
Qichen begins a four-day visit to Portugal on January 18.
